lesson_title: Micro Practice Run: Every Graph Is a Procedure
hook_text: Cost curves scare everyone — until you learn they're checklists, not artwork.
clip_script: Micro practice run, and here is the secret: every graph is a procedure, not a picture. The monopolist: find where marginal cost crosses marginal revenue — that is your quantity, eighty units. Read straight UP to the demand curve — that is your price, two hundred rand. Average cost at the same quantity: one sixty. Now it is arithmetic: two hundred minus one sixty is forty rand per unit, times eighty — three thousand two hundred rand of economic profit. Same procedure every time; only the gap changes direction. Inflation? Also a procedure: new index minus old, over the OLD one, times a hundred — one three nine comma one minus one thirty, over one thirty — seven percent. Divide by the new index and you hand back the marks. Weighted basket: weight times increase, added up — four plus one comma five plus nought comma six — six comma one percent. And the essay is four boxes: define for 2, contrast for 20, judge for 6, close fresh for 2. Learn the procedures, and the graphs stop being art you admire and become marks you collect.
visual_style: A monopoly graph assembling itself step by step with a glowing vertical line from equilibrium up to the price; number sentences stamping in like a till receipt; a weighted basket filling with groceries sized by their weights; the essay as four boxes filling 2, 20, 6, 2.
pacing: A deliberate step-by-step beat on the graph procedure, quickening through the inflation arithmetic, landing on a confident four-count for the essay boxes.
call_to_action: Do the full practice run and turn every graph you feared into a procedure you own.
